arcs.title: First Light
arcs.description: Nobody starts as an adventurer. They start by going outside, and then going a little further than last time. Three rides, in order, and the map is no longer only the bit you already knew.

quests.title: Out of the Door
quests.description: The hardest part of every ride is the first hundred metres. Take a road you have never taken — any road, as long as it is new to you — and the rest of the map starts to owe you something.

quests.title: Something Green
quests.description: Every town keeps a green place, and most riders pass the turning for years without taking it. Take it, then come home the way you like.

quests.title: Somewhere to Look From
quests.description: Ground you have ridden looks different from above it. Climb to somewhere you can see it from, and the first light of this is done.

arcs.title: The Edge of the Map
arcs.description: An Explorer's map has an edge, and the edge moves. This is the work of moving it: out past the fog, across three unknown places, and back with the shape of them.

quests.title: Past the Fog
quests.description: Roads you have never travelled, and enough of them to be sure it was deliberate. The fog does not lift for a rider who turns back at the first unfamiliar junction.

quests.title: Three Unknowns
quests.description: One unknown place is an accident. Three, in one ride, is a survey.

quests.title: And Back Again
quests.description: The edge is only moved once you can find your way home from it. Out to the far place, and back under your own navigation.

arcs.title: What the Stones Remember
arcs.description: A Wizard reads the city as a text somebody else wrote. Markers nobody explains, lines that are too straight to be accidents, ground older than the road on top of it.

quests.title: The Marker
quests.description: Somebody put it there and meant something by it. Stand at it, and write down what you think they meant.

quests.title: The Straight Idea
quests.description: Three points on one bearing. Ride them in any order; the line does not care, but you will see it once you have.

quests.title: Older Than the Road
quests.description: The tarmac is new. What it runs past is not. Find the old ground, and take a way there nobody has mapped for you.

arcs.title: The Iron Hours
arcs.description: A Warrior's arc is not about places. It is about the hours: holding a pace, paying a hill what it asks, and staying on the bike after the interesting part is over.

quests.title: The Tempo
quests.description: Not a sprint. A speed you can hold while you think about something else, held for long enough that it stops being comfortable.

quests.title: The Hill's Toll
quests.description: Every hill charges the same price and does not negotiate. Climb until it is paid.

quests.title: The Hour of Iron
quests.description: The last one is only time. Stay out in it, keep turning the pedals, and come back having done the unremarkable thing well.

arcs.title: A Record of Small Things
arcs.description: A Scribe's claim is that the small things are the record: one place looked at properly, three corners of a neighbourhood, a road nobody has written down. Ride it, photograph it, say what it was.

quests.title: One Place, Properly
quests.description: Not a glance from the saddle. Stop, photograph it, and write the thing about it that a photograph does not carry.

quests.title: Three Corners
quests.description: A neighbourhood is not one place. Take its corners, and note what changes between them.

quests.title: The Unwritten Road
quests.description: Roads you have never travelled, surveyed rather than merely ridden: the photograph, the note, and the distance to earn them.
